newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Camargo Correa to focus on infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Camargo Correa to focus on infrastructure.

text.p: Brazil's Grupo Camargo Correa said the sale of a 51 percent stake in its Banco Geral do Comercio to Spain's Banco Santander is part of the group's strategy to focus on its infrastructure businesses.
"Our core business is the infrastructure sector," said a spokesman for Grupo Camargo Correa.

However, he noted Camargo Correa, which owned 100 percent of Banco Geral, had decided to retain a minority stake in the bank because "it was not the group's interest to completely abandon the financial business."
Earlier Spain's largest bank Banco Santander announced it had bought a 51 percent controlling stake in Banco Geral do Comercio.

The bank said the transaction, which is subject to final approval by the Brazilian and Spanish authorities, would involve a maximum investment of about $220 million via capital increases to be paid over a three-year period.

The spokesman for Camargo Correa said the group, which has been restructuring, has made it a priority to take advantage of privatization opportunities in the power, transportation, sewage and telecommunications sectors.
The group has joined forces with Italy's Stet to bid for a concession to operate Band B cellular services.
It also will participate in today's auction of Brazilian power utility Dynamis Energetica, formerly known as Nacional Energetica.
Grupo Camargo Correa is one of Brazil's largest conglomerates, with interests in construction, engineering, sewage, cement, textile and metalurgy sectors.
The group has net revenues of $1.6 billion a year, while its net worth amounts to about $2.7 billion, the group said in a statement.
Camargo Correa bought a stake in Banco Geral do Comercio in 1964. Eight years later, the group acquired control of the bank, which has been focusing on small and medium-sized companies.
In 1996, Banco Geral's pro-forma consolidated assets totalled $1.2 billion, of which $575 million was in loans.
The bank has 77 branches and was recently authorized by the Brazilian government to expand its network to 200 branches.
